channel.title: The Daily Download
channel.description: Daily tech newsletters, with the linked articles read and turned into one episode.
channel.itunes:author: The Daily Download

item.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026
item.description: Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 as its IPO roadshow begins: what's new, how it scores, why it can cost more per task, and Ethan Mollick's "jagged AGI" verdict. Plus: Anthropic buys gas generators, Google's new TPUs, when the US imports tokens, the software IP writedown, how Product Hunt almost died, and quick hits.

item.title: Monday, November 9, 2026
item.description: Is AI already dramatically speeding up AI research? Ajeya Cotra makes the case, and an AI system proves the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture. Plus: Anthropic and OpenAI valuations slide, how to handle AI gross margins, Anthropic on agent memory and "dreaming", essays on signal collapse and the Jevons paradox, Nvidia's investigation, and quick hits.

item.title: Friday, November 6, 2026
item.description: Investors push back on Anthropic's IPO valuation, and METR finds AI has roughly doubled the pace of Anthropic's research. Plus: Gemini 4 Carbon tops a major leaderboard, a wave of new models, how AI made exploits cheap, GitHub rebuilding Git storage for agents, the end of feature discovery, and quick hits.

item.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026
item.description: Anthropic made $17 billion in a quarter, but its growth slowed and short-term GPU costs turned a profit into a loss. SaaStr and Tomasz Tunguz explain why, and why multi-year AI contracts are coming. Plus: PostHog moves off DuckDB, Airbnb's small fine-tuned classifier matches frontier models at 1% of the cost, Maggie Appleton on speculative design, and quick hits.

item.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026
item.description: Siri AI opens to developers as ChatGPT reaches 1.2 billion weekly users. Menlo's state of enterprise AI, a SaaS slowdown in Stripe data, what tokens really cost and Revolut's self-hosting savings, a second critique of the weights-editing paper, Anthropic's provable inference, plus three engineering deep dives: a tale of two eras, Netflix's performance agents, and how Nemotron stays cheap.

item.title: Tuesday, November 3, 2026
item.description: Anthropic's amended IPO filing says it may soon hit its threshold for AI-accelerated progress, and reports $33B in nine-month revenue. Plus the debate over models editing neural network weights directly, Claude message threads, the case for agents with one tool, Microsoft's Copilot Cowork lessons, Karri Saarinen on organizations overwhelmed by their own output, a16z on AI app premiums, and quick hits.

item.title: Monday, November 2, 2026
item.description: Wall Street gets nervous about AI spending as Google says AI Mode hurt search revenue, OpenAI raises less than hoped, and Anthropic's S-1 shows its first profitable quarter. Plus a correction on the Claude Code extension story, new Claude Ultra limits, three safety papers on hidden failure modes, Frank Calegari on how mathematics has changed, Postgres 19's AI-driven delay, hiring junior engineers, and quick hits.

item.title: Friday, October 30, 2026
item.description: Mistral Large 4 ships as trillion-parameter open weights, and Epoch shows an open model turning published Firefox fixes into exploits for about $1,000 each. Then The Batch's Halloween review of 2026's AI fears, DeepMind on the economics of intelligence, Noah Smith on a golden age of science, leadership in agent swarms, Meta's just-in-time tests, PM at Anthropic, and quick hits including DoorDash buying Instacart.

item.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon tops the leaderboards and goes to cyber defenders first, Nathan Lambert on the benchmarker's dilemma, AI-built games that are finally fun, Anthropic's new enterprise reports, and the future of the firm.

item.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026
item.description: Anthropic's $80B loss explained, Claude and OpenAI both claim to disprove the Exponential Time Hypothesis, AI agents formally verify the longest proof ever written, Claude in drug development, Genie 4, and the end of the coding interview.

item.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026
item.description: Anthropic files for its IPO and what the S-1 numbers say, how the Claude Code team reviews code at scale, an open model that tried to phone home, OpenAI's big math claims, robot arms doubling every 54 days, and tokens over hires.

item.title: Monday, October 26, 2026
item.description: Kimi K3.1 Pro nears the frontier with open weights promised, the OpenAI and Anthropic price war, Black October in security, Apple's 20B on-device model, an old network beating frontier models at skin cancer, and more.

item.title: Friday, October 23, 2026
item.description: Claude formally proves 123 libraries can't crash, METR red-teams OpenAI's agent monitor, Claude's text watermark, Anthropic's own source control, Meta's open Muse model and more.

item.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026
item.description: PHP2Shell and a very bad security day, Anthropic's Claude Duet, the Flint local coding model, AI models hiding messages in pictures, and Terry Tao's blog on young mathematicians.

item.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026
item.description: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, Claude designs scorpion-toxin binders, METR reviews Anthropic's risk report, Pichai, Mollick, the end of Foursquare and more.

item.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026
item.description: AI proves the quasi-Riemann hypothesis, Jack Clark tells the IMF the singularity has begun, why benchmarks mislead, and a wave of fast, cheap models.

item.title: Monday, October 19, 2026
item.description: How AI is changing work at Anthropic, Replit switches to OpenAI, the AI pricing maze, and whether AI brings a golden or dark age for mathematics.

item.title: Friday, October 16, 2026
item.description: Neural networks may be cleaner than we thought, Meta's Muse Spark Open, how Codex happened, what AI really costs, and a quantum milestone.

item.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026
item.description: Anthropic's $16.8B quarter and Ramp's AI spending data, Gemini Argon's monitorability problem, the $30 H100 test for AGI, agentic verification, Claude agent tracing, Google Deep Review, AI routers, and engineering stories from Cloudflare, GitHub, Meta and Netflix.

item.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026
item.description: Gemini 4 Argon goes wide, Anthropic replaces git with Scion, Claude agent flows, autonomy for financial agents, Apple HomeView, AI pricing, PostHog's 38 lessons, and a vision chip for Stargardt disease.
